page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The hardware includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes. The instance also delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 138344.04 and a PassMark CPU score of 123092.36. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier status for both small-block cached reads at 10215.75 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 393.15 GB/sec. The processor support for Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions drives top-tier performance in specialized tasks, including LLM prompt processing and multi-threaded decompression.

From a resource density perspective, the c8id.32xlarge offers high compute and local storage density, though its memory-to-vCPU ratio is relatively low at 2.0 GB per core. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring intensive CPU calculations paired with high-speed local storage, rather than massive memory footprints. It is suited for high-throughput database operations, Redis deployments, static web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 128 vCPUs, 64 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores running at 3.9 GHz, and 256.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory. It includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmarks indicate exceptional throughput for database operations, Redis SET actions, and multi-threaded decompression. While highly cost-efficient for raw compute and storage-heavy tasks, its 2.0 GB per core memory allocation represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications. This instance is optimized for high-performance computing, database hosting, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference.
